name: CTET Paper 2 (Maths & Science)
fullName: Central Teacher Eligibility Test – Paper II (Elementary Stage, Classes VI–VIII), Mathematics & Science stream
frequency: Usually twice a year (sessions are sometimes skipped or shifted)
approxCandidates: ≈18.7 lakh appeared for Paper 2, both streams combined, in the Feb 2026 session (Papers 1 + 2 together: 26.5 lakh registered, 23.2 lakh appeared)
eligibility: Graduation (50%) plus B.Ed, or Graduation plus a 2-year D.El.Ed, or a 4-year integrated B.A./B.Sc.Ed or B.El.Ed (final-year students may apply), as per NCTE norms. No upper age limit, and the certificate is valid for life.

pattern.notes: Real paper: 150 MCQs of 1 mark each, no negative marking, 2½ hours. Qualifying marks are 60% (90/150) for General and 55% (82/150) for SC/ST/OBC/PwD. Officially, 'Mathematics & Science' is a single 60-question section (30 Maths + 30 Science). It is split into two sections here only for analysis. Within each subject, about 20 questions test content (NCERT Classes VI–VIII) and 10 test pedagogy. This mock uses English as Language I and Hindi as Language II, and the languages must differ. The question bank holds 60 original questions (CDP 12, English 10, Hindi 8, Maths 15, Science 15), so a mock built from it is a scaled-down version of the full paper.

trendAnalysis.summary: This analysis covers the Jul 2024, Dec 2024 and Feb 2026 sessions. No CTET exam was held in calendar 2025: the Dec-2025 cycle was conducted on 8 Feb 2026. Paper 2 is consistently tougher than Paper 1, with only 18.56% passing in Feb 2026. The Maths & Science section is the most time-consuming: Maths content leans on geometry (angles, triangles, polygons, symmetry), integers/fractions and simple algebra, while Science content is drawn from NCERT Class VI–VIII topics (materials, the living world, electricity & magnets, light). Pedagogy questions now use classroom scenarios, for example van Hiele levels, error analysis, inquiry-based science and process skills. CDP for Paper 2 emphasises adolescence, Kohlberg, inclusive education (RPwD Act 2016) and NEP-2020 aligned assessment.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of intrinsic motivation?
options: A student studies hard to win a cash prize
A student solves extra puzzles because she enjoys the challenge
A student revises only because marks will be displayed on the notice board
A student completes homework to avoid a scolding
questions.explanation: Intrinsic motivation comes from interest or enjoyment in the task itself. Prizes, avoiding punishment and public recognition are all external (extrinsic) motivators.

relevance.note: Intrinsic vs extrinsic examples; CTET motivation item, options neatly built from extrinsic rewards

questions.question: According to Vygotsky, children talking aloud to themselves while solving a problem ('private speech'):
options: Should be strictly discouraged in class
Is a sign of a speech disorder
Shows cognitive immaturity and serves no purpose
Helps them guide and regulate their own thinking
questions.explanation: Vygotsky saw private speech as a tool for self-regulation that gradually becomes inner speech. Piaget, by contrast, considered egocentric speech to be non-functional.

relevance.note: Vygotsky private speech as self-regulation vs Piaget's egocentric-speech view; CTET favourite

questions.question: A 13-year-old can reason, "If all metals conduct electricity and X is a metal, then X conducts electricity," and can systematically test hypotheses. According to Piaget, she is in the:
questions.explanation: Abstract, hypothetico-deductive reasoning develops in the formal operational stage (about 11 years onwards).

relevance.note: Syllogistic/hypothesis testing -> formal operational; CTET item, slightly easy

questions.question: An adolescent says, "We must obey traffic rules because society would collapse into chaos if everyone ignored laws." According to Kohlberg, this reasoning belongs to the:
questions.explanation: Upholding laws to maintain social order is Stage 4 (conventional level). Stage 5 (social contract) sees laws as agreements that can be changed for the greater good.

relevance.note: 'Society would collapse' -> law and order with social-contract trap; precise Kohlberg item

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a component of Robert Sternberg's triarchic theory of intelligence?
questions.explanation: Sternberg's three components are analytical (componential), creative (experiential) and practical (contextual). Emotional intelligence was popularised by Salovey, Mayer and Goleman.

relevance.note: Sternberg triarchic NOT-component (EI trap); CTET intelligence item

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer.

"Bamboo is often mistaken for a tree, but it is actually a grass – the largest member of the grass family. Some species can grow nearly a metre in a single day, making bamboo one of the fastest-growing plants on Earth. Because it regenerates from its own roots after harvesting, it does not need to be replanted. Builders in north-east India have used it for centuries to make homes, bridges and scaffolding, and today engineers are studying how it might replace steel in low-cost housing. However, untreated bamboo is vulnerable to insects and moisture, so it must be seasoned carefully before use."

According to the passage, bamboo does not need to be replanted because:
options: It regenerates from its own roots after harvesting
Builders reuse the same bamboo for many years
It belongs to the tree family
It is naturally resistant to insects
questions.explanation: The passage states that bamboo 'regenerates from its own roots after harvesting', so it does not need to be replanted.

relevance.note: Reason stated in passage with passage-word distractors; CTET format

questions.question:
गद्यांश पढ़कर प्रश्न का उत्तर दीजिए।

क्योंकि वे बिना स्वार्थ के ज्ञान देती हैं
क्योंकि वे परीक्षा में अंक दिलाती हैं

questions.question: ₹720 is divided between two friends in the ratio 4 : 5. What is the larger share?

questions.question: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. What is the largest angle?
questions.explanation: The angles are 2k + 3k + 4k = 180°, so k = 20°. Largest angle = 4 × 20° = 80°.

relevance.note: Angle ratio 2:3:4 -> 80°; CTET geometry item

questions.question: What is the measure of each interior angle of a regular hexagon?
questions.explanation: Sum of interior angles = (6 − 2) × 180° = 720°. Each angle = 720° ÷ 6 = 120°.

questions.question: A polyhedron has 8 vertices and 12 edges. How many faces does it have?

questions.question: What is the median of the data 3, 8, 5, 12, 7, 10?
questions.explanation: Arranged in order: 3, 5, 7, 8, 10, 12. With an even count, the median is the mean of the 3rd and 4th values: (7 + 8) ÷ 2 = 7.5.

questions.question: A Class VI student says, "A rectangle has four right angles and opposite sides equal," but insists that a square cannot be a rectangle. According to the van Hiele model, the student is at the level of:

questions.question: A student simplifies 3(x + 4) as 3x + 4. The error shows that the student:
options: Has not correctly applied the distributive property

questions.explanation: For Piaget, thought comes first and language mirrors the child's cognitive development. The view that language shapes thought, and the role of private speech, belong to Vygotsky.

questions.question: In a Class 7 science project, which practice best helps to counter gender stereotypes?
options: Giving girls extra marks to encourage them in science
Letting students choose their roles freely, without any guidance from the teacher
Forming separate groups of boys and girls so that each feels comfortable
Rotating roles so that every student handles apparatus, records data and presents the findings
questions.explanation: Rotating roles ensures that girls and boys alike experience hands-on and leadership tasks. Free choice often reproduces stereotypes; segregation and extra marks reinforce difference.

questions.question: Students compare their own science reports with a rubric, identify what they need to improve and set goals for the next report. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: When learners themselves monitor and regulate their learning through self-assessment, it is assessment as learning.

questions.question: Which of the following is the best example of a competency-based assessment item in Class 8 science, as envisaged by NEP 2020?
options: Plan an investigation to find out whether the colour of light affects the growth of plants.
List the parts of a flower.
Fill in the blank: Chlorophyll is found in ____.
questions.explanation: Competency-based items require applying concepts and skills in a new situation – here, planning a fair test. The others test recall.

questions.topic: Inclusive Education & Children with Special Needs
questions.question: A Class 6 student avoids eye contact, finds it hard to understand jokes and social cues, insists on following exactly the same routine every day and becomes very upset by sudden changes. These signs are most typical of:
questions.explanation: Difficulties in social communication combined with restricted, repetitive behaviours and insistence on sameness are characteristic of autism spectrum disorder.

questions.topic: Inclusive Education & Children with Special Needs
questions.question: Which is the most appropriate support for a Class 7 student with low vision in an inclusive classroom?
options: Providing large-print or tactile material and reading aloud what is written on the board
Excusing her from all tasks that involve diagrams
Seating her at the back so that her aids do not disturb others
Asking a classmate to complete her written work for her
questions.explanation: Accessible formats and verbalising board work allow her to take part fully. Excusing her or having others do her work lowers expectations and denies her learning.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): When a student says that plants take in their food from the soil, the teacher should first explore why the student thinks so.
Reason (R): Students' alternative conceptions are usually based on their own reasoning and experiences.

Choose the correct option.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Alternative conceptions make sense to students because they arise from experience (plants are seen growing in soil). Exploring that reasoning lets the teacher create cognitive conflict and conceptual change. R explains A.

questions.question: After failing a test, a student says, "I failed because the paper was too difficult." According to Weiner's attribution theory, the student attributes failure to a cause that is:
questions.explanation: Task difficulty is external, relatively stable and outside the student's control. Effort is internal and controllable, ability is internal and stable, and luck is external and unstable.

questions.question: Before solving a problem, a student asks herself, "What do I already know? Which strategy should I use?" Afterwards she checks whether the strategy worked. She is using:
questions.explanation: Planning, monitoring and evaluating one's own thinking is metacognition – thinking about one's own thinking.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer.

"Two summers ago, a group of schoolchildren in a small town noticed that the sparrows which used to nest under the eaves of their school had disappeared. Their science teacher, instead of giving them an answer, asked them to find out why. Over the next few months the students turned detectives. They counted birds on their way to school, interviewed shopkeepers and grandparents, and compared old photographs of the market with new ones. Slowly a picture emerged. The old houses, with gaps in their tiled roofs and wooden beams, had been replaced by smooth concrete buildings that offered no place to nest. Kitchen gardens, once full of the insects that sparrow chicks depend on, had been paved over for parking. Even the grain shops, which once spilt a few seeds on the ground every day, now sold everything in sealed plastic packets.

The students did not stop at finding causes. They built wooden nest boxes, persuaded the municipal office to leave a strip of the school ground unpaved, and planted native shrubs that attract insects. By the following spring, three pairs of sparrows had moved into the boxes. The number was small, but the students had learnt something that no textbook could have taught them so well: that the disappearance of an ordinary bird can be a signal of larger changes in the way we live."

According to the passage, the sparrows could no longer nest in the town because:
options: grain was now sold in sealed plastic packets
kitchen gardens had been paved over for parking
old houses with gaps in their roofs had been replaced by smooth concrete buildings
the students had disturbed the nests under the eaves
questions.explanation: The passage says the concrete buildings 'offered no place to nest'. Sealed packets and paved gardens affected food (seeds and insects), not nesting sites.

"I am the road that the village made
Of footsteps pressed in sun and shade;
I carry the farmer, I carry the cart,
I carry the songs of a lonely heart.
They cover me now with stone and tar,
And trucks roar by from cities far;
But still at dusk, when the noise has gone,
I hear the old footsteps walking on."

What change has come to the road, according to the poem?
options: It has become narrower and full of footsteps
It has been closed for farmers and carts
It has been covered with stone and tar, and trucks now pass on it
It has been moved closer to the city
questions.explanation: 'They cover me now with stone and tar, / And trucks roar by from cities far' – the road has been paved and carries heavy traffic.

options: comprehensible but slightly beyond their present level
exactly at their present level, so that they feel confident
authentic material well beyond their present level
questions.explanation: Krashen's 'i + 1': input that is understandable yet contains structures a little beyond the learner's current competence leads to acquisition.

questions.explanation: Learners use language to complete a meaningful, real-world task, with focus on form coming after the task. This is task-based language teaching, a communicative approach.

options: A comprehension passage written for the textbook exercise
A local railway timetable or a newspaper report
A list of difficult words prepared by the teacher
questions.explanation: Authentic materials are texts produced for real-life purposes, not for language teaching – such as timetables, newspapers, menus and brochures.

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate way to assess the speaking skills of Class 6 students in a large class?
options: A single oral test at the end of the year with marks only for pronunciation
A written test on the rules of conversation
Recitation of memorised dialogues from the textbook
Paired and group tasks such as role plays, observed with a rubric over several weeks
questions.explanation: Speaking is best assessed through real interaction over time using clear criteria (fluency, appropriateness, vocabulary, etc.). Recitation tests memory, not speaking ability.

questions.topic: Challenges of Teaching in Multilingual Classrooms

options: a sign of weak proficiency in both languages
an error that must be corrected at once
a natural part of learning in a multilingual setting that can be built upon
a reason to insist that only English be spoken in class
questions.explanation: Moving between languages (translanguaging) is natural for multilingual learners and can be used as a resource to build both languages.

"दादी कहती थीं कि हमारे गाँव का मेला केवल ख़रीदारी की जगह नहीं था, वह लोगों के मिलने का बहाना था। दूर-दूर के गाँवों से लोग बैलगाड़ियों में आते, रिश्तेदारों से मिलते, कुम्हारों से मिट्टी के बर्तन और लोहारों से खेती के औज़ार ख़रीदते। शाम होते ही कठपुतली का खेल शुरू होता और बच्चे-बूढ़े सब एक साथ हँसते। अब मेला सिमट गया है। सड़कें पक्की हो गई हैं, गाँव-गाँव में दुकानें खुल गई हैं और मोबाइल पर रिश्तेदारों से रोज़ बात हो जाती है। सुविधाएँ बढ़ी हैं, इसमें कोई संदेह नहीं, पर दादी को लगता है कि आमने-सामने बैठकर बतियाने का जो सुख था, वह किसी स्क्रीन से नहीं मिल सकता।"

गद्यांश में प्रयुक्त 'संदेह' शब्द का पर्यायवाची है —
questions.explanation: 'संदेह' का पर्यायवाची 'शंका' है। 'आस्था' इसका विलोम-सा अर्थ देता है; 'संकेत' और 'संताप' ध्वनि-साम्य वाले भ्रामक शब्द हैं।

questions.question:
अभिकथन (A): बच्चों की भाषायी त्रुटियाँ उनके भाषा-विकास की प्रक्रिया का स्वाभाविक हिस्सा हैं।
तर्क (R): त्रुटियाँ दर्शाती हैं कि बच्चा भाषा के नियमों के बारे में अपनी परिकल्पनाएँ बनाकर उनका परीक्षण कर रहा है।

सही विकल्प चुनिए।
options: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं तथा (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
(A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं, परंतु (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
questions.explanation: बच्चे भाषा के नियमों का अनुमान लगाकर उन्हें प्रयोग में परखते हैं; इसी क्रम में त्रुटियाँ होती हैं। इसलिए त्रुटियाँ सीखने की स्वाभाविक प्रक्रिया हैं — (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या है।

questions.question: भाषा-कक्षा में समूह-चर्चा, नाटक और साथियों से बातचीत के भरपूर अवसर देना किसके विचारों के सबसे अधिक अनुरूप है?
questions.explanation: वाइगोत्स्की के अनुसार भाषा और चिंतन का विकास सामाजिक अंतःक्रिया से होता है। चॉम्स्की जन्मजात क्षमता पर और स्किनर अनुकरण-पुनर्बलन पर बल देते हैं।

questions.question: कक्षा 7 में 'पढ़कर समझने' की क्षमता विकसित करने के लिए सबसे उपयुक्त तरीका है —
options: पाठ का सस्वर वाचन कराकर उच्चारण की अशुद्धियाँ ठीक करना
पाठ के कठिन शब्दों के अर्थ पहले से लिखवा देना
पढ़ने से पहले विषय पर चर्चा करना, पढ़ते समय अनुमान लगवाना और बाद में अपने अनुभवों से जोड़कर बातचीत करना
पाठ के प्रश्नों के उत्तर पुस्तक में खोजकर लिखवाना
questions.explanation: पूर्व-ज्ञान को सक्रिय करना, अनुमान लगाना और पाठ को अनुभव से जोड़ना अर्थग्रहण की रणनीतियाँ हैं। अन्य विकल्प उच्चारण या सूचना-खोज तक सीमित हैं।

questions.question: कक्षा 8 के विद्यार्थियों में सुनकर समझने का कौशल विकसित करने के लिए सबसे उपयुक्त गतिविधि है —
options: रेडियो पर कोई समाचार या वार्ता सुनकर उसके मुख्य बिंदुओं पर चर्चा करना
questions.explanation: वास्तविक सामग्री सुनकर उसके मुख्य बिंदु पहचानना सुनकर अर्थग्रहण को विकसित करता है। श्रुतलेख मुख्यतः वर्तनी और लेखन का अभ्यास है।

questions.question: कक्षा 7 में विद्यार्थियों के लेखन-कौशल के सतत आकलन का सबसे उपयुक्त तरीका है —
options: सत्र के अंत में एक निबंध-परीक्षा लेना
पत्र, डायरी, कहानी आदि लेखन-नमूनों का संग्रह (पोर्टफोलियो) बनाकर समय के साथ प्रगति देखना
questions.explanation: विभिन्न विधाओं में समय-समय पर किए गए लेखन का पोर्टफोलियो विद्यार्थी की प्रगति को लगातार दिखाता है, जो सतत आकलन का मूल भाव है।

questions.question: एक कहानी पढ़ाने के बाद शिक्षक बच्चों की कल्पनाशीलता और अभिव्यक्ति का आकलन करना चाहता है। इसके लिए सबसे उपयुक्त प्रश्न है —
options: यदि आप कहानी का अंत बदल सकते, तो क्या बदलते और क्यों?
कहानी में कौन-कौन सी घटनाएँ हुईं, क्रम से लिखिए।
कहानी के कठिन शब्दों के अर्थ लिखिए।
कहानी के मुख्य पात्र का नाम लिखिए।
questions.explanation: खुले प्रश्न का कोई एक निश्चित उत्तर नहीं होता; बच्चा कल्पना करता है और अपने तर्क व्यक्त करता है। अन्य प्रश्न स्मरण पर आधारित हैं।

questions.question: कक्षा 6 के कई बच्चे 'कृपा', 'कृषि' जैसे शब्दों को 'क्रिपा', 'क्रिषि' लिखते हैं। इसके लिए सबसे उपयुक्त उपचारात्मक उपाय है —
options: अशुद्ध शब्दों को बीस-बीस बार लिखवाना
'ऋ' की मात्रा वाले शब्दों से युक्त रोचक पठन-सामग्री, शब्द-खेल और शब्दकोश से स्वयं जाँच के अवसर देना
ऋ और रि के उच्चारण के नियम कंठस्थ कराना
इन त्रुटियों पर अंक काटना ताकि बच्चे सावधान रहें
questions.explanation: शब्दों से बार-बार सार्थक संदर्भ में परिचय और स्वयं जाँचने का अवसर वर्तनी की समझ बनाते हैं। बार-बार लिखवाना या अंक काटना यांत्रिक और भयकारी उपाय हैं।

questions.question: एक कक्षा में बच्चे हिंदी, उर्दू, बांग्ला और संथाली बोलते हैं। शिक्षक 'पानी', 'माँ' जैसे शब्द इन भाषाओं में कैसे बोले जाते हैं, इस पर चर्चा कराता है। इसका मुख्य उद्देश्य है —
options: हिंदी सीखने के समय को कम करना
बच्चों में भाषा के प्रति जागरूकता और भाषायी विविधता के प्रति सम्मान विकसित करना
बच्चों के शब्द-ज्ञान की परीक्षा लेना
questions.explanation: विभिन्न भाषाओं की तुलना से बच्चे भाषा की संरचना पर ध्यान देते हैं और सभी भाषाओं को सम्मान से देखना सीखते हैं — बहुभाषिकता संसाधन बनती है।

questions.question: कक्षा 7 में मुहावरों का शिक्षण करने का सबसे उपयुक्त तरीका है —
options: कहानियों और समाचारों में आए मुहावरों को पहचानकर संदर्भ में उनके अर्थ पर चर्चा करना और अपने वाक्यों में प्रयोग कराना
मुहावरों और उनके अर्थों की सूची कंठस्थ कराना
परीक्षा में अक्सर पूछे जाने वाले मुहावरों का अभ्यास कराना
questions.explanation: मुहावरे का अर्थ संदर्भ से खुलता है। प्रयोग और संदर्भ के माध्यम से सीखना स्थायी होता है, जबकि सूचियाँ रटाना यांत्रिक है।

questions.question: What is the smallest number by which 2560 must be divided so that the quotient is a perfect cube?
questions.explanation: 2560 = 2⁹ × 5. 2⁹ = (2³)³ is already a perfect cube, so divide by 5: 2560 ÷ 5 = 512 = 8³.

questions.question: The value of (2⁻¹ + 3⁻¹)⁻¹ is:
questions.explanation: 2⁻¹ + 3⁻¹ = 1/2 + 1/3 = 5/6, and (5/6)⁻¹ = 6/5. Writing (2 + 3)⁻¹ = 1/5 or 2 + 3 = 5 are common errors.

questions.question: A shopkeeper marks an article 25% above its cost price and then allows a discount of 10% on the marked price. His profit per cent is:
questions.explanation: Let CP = 100. MP = 125; SP = 125 × 0.9 = 112.5. Profit = 12.5%. 25% − 10% = 15% is the common shortcut error.

questions.question: If x + 1/x = 5, then the value of x² + 1/x² is:
questions.explanation: (x + 1/x)² = x² + 2 + 1/x², so x² + 1/x² = 25 − 2 = 23. Forgetting the 2 gives 25; adding it gives 27.

questions.question: Each interior angle of a regular polygon measures 144°. How many sides does the polygon have?
questions.explanation: Each exterior angle = 180° − 144° = 36°. Number of sides = 360° ÷ 36° = 10.

questions.question: Which of the following sets of lengths can be the sides of a right-angled triangle?
The circumference of a circle is 88 cm. Its area is (take π = 22/7):
questions.explanation: 2πr = 88 ⇒ r = 14 cm. Area = (22/7) × 14 × 14 = 616 cm². 1232 (= 2πr × r) and 308 come from mixing up the circumference and area formulas.

questions.question: How many cubes of edge 3 cm can be cut from a cuboid measuring 18 cm × 12 cm × 9 cm?
questions.explanation: Along the edges: 18/3 = 6, 12/3 = 4, 9/3 = 3; number of cubes = 6 × 4 × 3 = 72 (equivalently 1944 ÷ 27).

questions.question: In a pie chart showing how 720 students travel to school, the sector for 'bus' has an angle of 90°. How many students travel by bus?
Several Class 8 students write a² × a³ = a⁶. Which is the most effective remedial strategy?
options: Ask them to memorise the law aᵐ × aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ and repeat it daily
Give them twenty more questions of the same type
Have them write a² × a³ as (a × a) × (a × a × a) and count the factors
Show them a chart of all the laws of exponents
questions.explanation: The students multiply exponents instead of adding them. Expanding the powers lets them see that there are 5 factors of a, building the meaning of the law rather than a rule to memorise.

questions.question: Which of the following deficiency diseases is correctly matched with its cause?
options: Night blindness – deficiency of vitamin B1
questions.explanation: Rickets is caused by lack of vitamin D. Beriberi is due to vitamin B1, night blindness to vitamin A, and goitre to iodine deficiency.

questions.question: A few drops of copper sulphate solution and caustic soda solution are added to a food sample, and the mixture turns violet. The food contains:
questions.explanation: A violet colour with copper sulphate and caustic soda shows the presence of protein. Starch gives blue-black with iodine and fat leaves an oily patch on paper.

questions.question: China rose indicator turns acidic solutions ______ and basic solutions ______.
questions.explanation: China rose indicator turns acids dark pink (magenta) and bases green. 'Colourless; pink' describes phenolphthalein.

questions.question: Which of the following involves both a physical change and a chemical change?
questions.explanation: Wax melts (physical change) and the vaporised wax burns to form carbon dioxide and water (chemical change). The others involve only one kind of change.

questions.question: An iron nail is kept in a blue solution of copper sulphate. After some time the solution turns light green and a brown coating forms on the nail. This happens because:
options: copper is more reactive than iron and displaces it
iron is more reactive than copper and displaces it from copper sulphate
the solution is heated by the nail
questions.explanation: Iron + copper sulphate → iron sulphate (green) + copper (brown deposit). A more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from its salt solution.

questions.question: Which fibre, obtained from wood pulp, is known as 'artificial silk'?
questions.explanation: Rayon is made from chemically treated wood pulp and resembles silk. Acrylic is called 'artificial wool'; nylon and polyester are made from petrochemicals.

questions.question: Water should NOT be used to put out a fire involving electrical equipment because:
options: water can conduct electricity and cause electric shock
water is lighter than the burning material
water increases the supply of oxygen
water does not lower the temperature of the burning material
questions.explanation: Water conducts electricity and can electrocute the person putting out the fire; carbon dioxide extinguishers are used instead. (Oil fires are another case where water should not be used, because oil floats on water.)

questions.question: Which pair of structures is found in plant cells but is generally absent in animal cells?
questions.explanation: Plant cells have a cell wall and plastids (e.g. chloroplasts); animal cells lack both. Nucleus, cell membrane and mitochondria occur in both.

questions.question: The digestion of carbohydrates begins in the:
questions.explanation: Salivary amylase in the mouth begins breaking starch into sugar. The stomach mainly digests proteins; carbohydrate digestion is completed in the small intestine.

questions.question: Which blood vessel carries blood poor in oxygen from the heart to the lungs?
questions.explanation: Arteries carry blood away from the heart. The pulmonary artery is the exception that carries oxygen-poor blood (to the lungs). The pulmonary vein brings oxygen-rich blood back to the heart.

questions.question: The changes that take place in boys at puberty, such as the growth of facial hair, are controlled by the hormone:
questions.explanation: Testosterone, released by the testes, brings about secondary sexual characters in boys. Oestrogen does so in girls.

questions.question: Which of the following diseases is correctly matched with the type of microorganism that causes it?
options: Foot and mouth disease (in cattle) – virus
questions.explanation: Foot and mouth disease is viral. Anthrax, citrus canker and cholera are all caused by bacteria.

questions.question: Which bacterium lives in the root nodules of leguminous plants and fixes atmospheric nitrogen?
questions.explanation: Rhizobium fixes nitrogen in the root nodules of legumes. Lactobacillus forms curd; yeast is a fungus.

questions.question: A car travels the first 60 km of a journey at 30 km/h and the next 60 km at 60 km/h. Its average speed for the whole journey is:
questions.explanation: Time = 60/30 + 60/60 = 2 + 1 = 3 h. Average speed = total distance/total time = 120/3 = 40 km/h. Averaging the two speeds (45 km/h) is the common error.

questions.question: Ball bearings are used between the moving parts of machines because:
options: they increase the friction between the parts
they make the parts heavier and more stable
rolling friction is much smaller than sliding friction
questions.explanation: Ball bearings replace sliding with rolling, and rolling friction is smaller than sliding friction. Friction is reduced, not removed completely.

questions.question: The deflection of a compass needle placed near a wire carrying electric current was first observed by:
questions.explanation: Oersted observed (1820) that a current-carrying wire deflects a compass needle, showing that an electric current produces a magnetic effect.

questions.question: The image formed by a convex mirror is always:
options: real, erect and of the same size
questions.explanation: A convex mirror always forms a virtual, erect and diminished image, which is why it is used as a rear-view mirror. Virtual, erect and enlarged images come from a concave mirror when the object is very close.

questions.question: A vibrating object produces a sound of frequency 500 Hz. The time period of its vibration is:
questions.explanation: Time period = 1/frequency = 1/500 s = 0.002 s.

questions.question: Which product obtained from petroleum refining is used for surfacing roads?
questions.explanation: Bitumen is used in paints and for road surfacing. Paraffin wax is used in candles and ointments, LPG as a fuel.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): A scientific theory that is strongly supported by evidence may still be modified in future.
Reason (R): Scientific knowledge is based on evidence, and new evidence can lead to its revision.

Choose the correct option.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Science is tentative: even well-supported theories remain open to revision when new evidence appears. R explains A.

questions.question: A teacher explains how ideas about the structure of the atom changed from Dalton to Thomson to Rutherford. According to NCF 2005, this addresses which validity of the science curriculum?
questions.explanation: Historical validity requires learners to see how scientific concepts evolve over time and the social context of science.

questions.question: After observing that a plant kept in a dark room has turned pale, a student says, "The plant is pale because it could not make chlorophyll without light." Which science process skill is the student using?
questions.explanation: Explaining an observation on the basis of what one knows is inferring. Observing is noting the pale colour; predicting is stating what will happen in future.

questions.question: Which task best assesses students' ability to design an experiment?
options: Asking students to plan an investigation on whether temperature affects the rate at which sugar dissolves, naming what they will change, measure and keep the same
Multiple-choice questions on the steps of the scientific method
Asking students to copy an experiment from the textbook into their notebooks
questions.explanation: Planning a fair test and identifying the independent, dependent and controlled variables directly assesses the skill of designing an experiment.

questions.question: Many Class 7 students believe that woollen clothes keep us warm because wool produces heat. Which activity would best help them change this idea?
options: Telling them the correct reason and asking them to write it five times
Showing pictures of sheep in cold places
Wrapping one bottle of warm water in wool and leaving another unwrapped, recording temperatures over time and then discussing the result
Asking them to memorise the definition of an insulator
questions.explanation: Students will find that the wrapped bottle cools more slowly but does not get warmer – wool traps air and reduces heat loss, it does not produce heat. Such cognitive conflict helps conceptual change.

pyqBlueprint.method: Compiled from the CTET papers of August 2023, January 2024, July 2024 and December 2024 (official question booklets/answer keys as reproduced on coaching sites) and memory-based shift analyses of the February 2026 cycle (no CTET was held in calendar 2025). WebSearch was used for the 2024–2026 analyses (PW, Careers360, Adda247, Prepp); full official papers could not be fetched, so the archetype list also draws on the writer's own knowledge of earlier CTET papers. Patterns are described in our own words; no real question is reproduced. Frequencies are per 30-question section.

archetypes.pattern: Scenario → principle of development (cephalocaudal, proximodistal, general-to-specific, continuity, individual differences, interrelated domains)
"Which statement about development is NOT correct" — stages of childhood/adolescence, development as qualitative and quantitative, lifelong
Nature–nurture: choose the correct statement about the interaction of heredity and environment
Agents of socialisation (family as primary, school/peers/media as secondary) and the teacher's role in socialisation
Child's behaviour → Piagetian stage feature (animism, egocentrism, centration, conservation, object permanence, hypothetico-deductive reasoning)
Piaget's processes: schema, assimilation, accommodation, equilibration identified from an example; distractors swap assimilation/accommodation
Vygotsky: ZPD, scaffolding, more knowledgeable other, private speech, cultural tools — concept from a classroom description
A child's moral reasoning statement → Kohlberg level/stage (punishment-obedience, instrumental, good boy–good girl, law and order, social contract)
Compare/critique the theorists (Piaget vs Vygotsky on language and learning, Gilligan's critique of Kohlberg) — pick the correct statement
Features of child-centred/progressive education and the teacher as facilitator (Dewey, NCF 2005)
Gardner's multiple intelligences from a child's profile; Sternberg's triarchic components; IQ basics
Relationship of language and thought: Vygotsky vs Piaget, Chomsky's LAD, private speech
Gender stereotypes in school practices/textbooks and the teacher's appropriate response; gender as a social construct
Individual differences: sources of diversity and how to address diverse learners (differentiated instruction)
Distinguish assessment of / for / as learning; purpose of CCE and formative vs summative assessment
Assessment tools and NEP 2020 ideas: portfolio, rubrics, open-ended questions, holistic progress card, competency-based assessment

Factual detail/reason stated in a 150–250-word prose passage; distractors use words from the passage with wrong links
Inference, "NOT supported by the passage" or central idea; trap = option true in general but not stated
Vocabulary in context: synonym/antonym of a word as used in the passage
Grammar item from the passage: part of speech, sentence type, tense/voice, phrase/clause
Literal meaning of a line/stanza of an unseen poem; "which does the poet NOT say"
Poetic device in a quoted line (metaphor, simile, personification, alliteration) or rhyme scheme
Tone/theme of the poem or meaning of a poetic word
Theorists of acquisition (Krashen's input/affective filter, Chomsky's LAD, Vygotsky) and acquisition vs learning; errors as part of learning
Identify a method/approach from a description (whole language, CLT, TPR, direct, grammar-translation, structural)
Best activity to develop listening or speaking at a given class level (role play, storytelling, listening for information)
Name the language sub-skill described (skimming, scanning, intensive vs extensive listening/reading)
Remedial step for a reading/writing difficulty, or choice of authentic/supplementary materials
What a given tool assesses or the best way to assess a skill (cloze, rubric, portfolio, oral tasks)
